name: TJUV
description: Tjuv (Swedish for 'Thief') is a fishing card game for two or more players. It is sometimes known as Tattare. Unlike traditional Casino, capturing is based on suit and rank hierarchy rather than numerical value. A unique feature is the ability to 'steal' captured piles from opponents if you have a matching card of higher rank.

content.text: Tjuv (Swedish for 'Thief') is a fishing card game for two or more players. It is sometimes known as Tattare. Unlike traditional Casino, capturing is based on suit and rank hierarchy rather than numerical value. A unique feature is the ability to 'steal' captured piles from opponents if you have a matching card of higher rank.

Tjuv (Thief), formerly known as Tattare, is a Swedish fishing game first documented in the 1922 rulebook Kortspelsregler till tidsfördriv och nöje (Wahlström & Widstrand). The name Tattare was a disparaging term for Romani and Swedish travellers; as a game name it alluded to an unjustified reputation for stealing. Ulf Schenkmanis used the name Tjuv in his 1988 book Kortspel & patienser. The game has remained a simple family and children's pastime in Sweden.
36-card deck: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 in each suit (no 2-5). Rank: A (high) to 6 (low).

Three cards to each player. Each player places their lowest card face up on the table (or one of equal lowest). With two players the dealer adds one card from the deck to the table; with three or more the dealer reduces the table to three cards then deals one more to each. Three cards face up on table; remainder forms the talon.

items.text: Schenkmanis table replenish: When fewer than three cards on table, player draws from talon and lays them face up on the table until three on table or talon empty (instead of laying from hand).
